title: Welcome to the board
instruction: Identify the case header, graph, query paper, evidence file and submission controls. GraphFrames and Zingg are visible but disabled until T2 — Connections Lab.
hint_text: The graph is the main workspace. Hovering or pressing the locked GraphFrames and Zingg controls explains that they are introduced in the next tutorial.

title: Select a node
instruction: Select Buster Bulldog to open the node detail panel.
hint_text: Nodes represent people, organizations, accounts, events or documents.

title: Read provenance
instruction: Review Buster’s source system and safe attributes.
hint_text: A record is only as meaningful as the source and fields that support it.

title: Read an arrow
instruction: Select the ASSIGNED_TO relationship from Buster to Register 2.
hint_text: Read from source to target: Buster was assigned to Register 2.

title: Ask a precise question
instruction: Use the suggested Genie query: “Show the records connected to the 120 BSC shortage.”
hint_text: The quote shows the cost before the query runs.

title: Reveal related records
instruction: Confirm the guided Genie query and let the graph add the relevant events and documents.
hint_text: A query adds records; it does not decide guilt.

title: Follow the chain
instruction: Trace Buster → manual opening → shortage and Buster → admission → shortage.
hint_text: The strongest conclusion uses access, action, loss and corroboration.

title: Pin evidence
instruction: Add the login, manual opening, shortage and admission message to the case file.
hint_text: Selecting a suspect is not enough; the submission needs supporting records.

title: Protect the reporter
instruction: Review Nell’s incident report and mark her as a protected reporter, not a suspect.
hint_text: Appearing near the incident does not make the reporter culpable.

title: Submit the case
instruction: Select Buster Bulldog as the suspect and submit the case.
hint_text: The attempt becomes immutable after submission.

title: Read the result
instruction: Review the score components and the six possible Academy endings.
hint_text: Accuracy, evidence, relationship reading, protected actors and efficiency all contribute.
